Check the setup of a Local Source

Source: R/local-source.R
og_local_check.Rd

Reports the Python a Local Source uses and how it was chosen, the reticulate and ogquery versions, the format series ogquery reads, and, for each path, the Store Release found there (for a GWAS Store directory, the one it resolved to), its store_id, release_id and format_version, and whether ogquery can read it. It reports problems instead of raising them, so it is the place to start when og_local() refuses: only a path that isn't a character vector of paths, or a Local Source, is an error.

Usage

og_local_check(path)

Arguments

path

The directory of each GWAS Store or Store Release, as for og_local(), or a Local Source.

Value

An og_local_check: a list with

  • python (the Python's path) and chosen_by (how it was chosen, as for og_local()'s errors: "RETICULATE_PYTHON", "use_python", "automatic", ...);

  • reticulate and ogquery, their versions (ogquery is the one found, even when opengwasr doesn't support it);

  • ogquery_required, the ogquery versions opengwasr supports (">=0.1.0,<1"), and ogquery_in_range, whether the ogquery found is one of them (NA when none is found);

  • reads, the format series ogquery reads, such as "0.3" (any 0.3.x);

  • releases, a data frame with one row per path: path (as given), release_path (the Store Release directory it resolved to: itself for a Store Release directory, the one a GWAS Store directory holds, or NA when it holds none or several, or the path doesn't exist or isn't a directory), store_id, release_id, format_version, readable, problem (NA, "not_release", "several", "format" or "unavailable") and reason;

  • duplicates, the GWAS Stores given more than one Store Release;

  • unavailable, the opengwasr_local_unavailable condition og_local() would raise, or NULL;

  • problems, all of that as sentences, for printing;

  • ld, the Local Source's PLINK Reference (as og_ld_resource() gives it), or NULL (paths given, or none).

Missing values are NA. An LD-only Local Source (og_local(bfile = )) has no Store Releases, so no Python is looked for: releases has no rows, python, ogquery and reads are NA, and it reports its PLINK Reference (its fileset, and the PLINK binary and version).

Details

Like og_local(), it finds Python on first use, so it sets Python up automatically when you haven't chosen one.

Examples

stores <- system.file("stores", package = "opengwasr")
og_local_check(file.path(stores, c("dense", "hyb")))
#> <og_local_check>
#> Python:     /opt/hostedtoolcache/Python/3.13.18/x64/bin/python (chosen by RETICULATE_PYTHON)
#> reticulate: 1.47.0
#> ogquery:    0.4.0, reads format 0.3.x
#> 
#> Store Releases:
#>   /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/dense
#>     resolved to /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/dense/r
#>     s/r, format 0.3.0: readable
#>   /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/opengwasr/stores/hyb
#>     not readable: 2 Store Releases one level down (hyb/v1 in v1, hyb/v1-completed in v1c); a GWAS Store directory holds one
